title: Refactor back-end to feature-based file structure
description:
Research basis:
- Fastify docs recommend plugin-based encapsulation and scoping routes/services by concern, which aligns with feature/domain-based organization.

Goal:
- Reorganize back-end source into feature modules so each domain owns routes, service logic, and related tests.

Target direction:
- src/features/content/...
- src/features/health/...
- src/features/hello/...
- src/core/... for cross-feature infrastructure (server config, security headers, rate limiting, shared utilities)
- entrypoint composes/registers feature plugins

Acceptance criteria:
1. Back-end files are grouped by feature/domain first.
2. Routes and feature-specific logic are colocated within feature modules.
3. Core infrastructure remains centralized and reusable.
4. Runtime behavior is unchanged (non-functional refactor).
5. Back-end tests, lint, typecheck, and build pass.

title: Docker: react-router not resolved after bun install on startup
description: After the startup bun install fix (website-ibv), Vite starts but fails dependency pre-bundling. It detects the lockfile changed (from the bind mount) and re-optimizes, but still cannot resolve react-router. Error: 'Failed to run dependency scan. Skipping dependency pre-bundling. react-router (imported by /app/front-end/src/components/TopBar.tsx) - Are they installed?' Likely the anonymous volume for /app/front-end/node_modules is still stale and the startup bun install only updates /app/node_modules at the root, not the workspace node_modules.
close_reason: Fixed two problems: (1) Removed anonymous volumes for workspace node_modules (/app/front-end/node_modules, /app/back-end/node_modules) from docker-compose.yml — these were overlaying the bind-mounted host directories with stale content. The host's node_modules (which has react-router) is now used directly via the bind mount. Kept the root /app/node_modules anonymous volume since root isn't bind-mounted. (2) Added missing workspace package.json to each Dockerfile dev stage (back-end/package.json in front-end, front-end/package.json in back-end) so the startup bun install can resolve all workspaces. Also removed the now-unnecessary COPY of workspace node_modules from deps stage.

title: Research continuous-scroll homepage pattern and define scaffold plan
description:
Research goals:
- Analyze a continuous homepage that progresses section-by-section while scrolling.
- Inspect reference implementations by reading source repositories instead of live domains:
  - https://github.com/projectbluefin/website
  - https://github.com/ublue-os/bazzite.gg

Research approach:
- Review information architecture, section sequencing, reusable components, and scroll/navigation patterns directly from repository code and assets.
- Extract implementation patterns suitable for this project's stack and current feature-based structure.

Research document (for review/proofreading):
- `homepage_continuous_scroll_scaffold_plan.md` (repo root)

Deliverable:
- A concrete implementation plan for this repo's homepage scaffolding (content can be placeholder), written to `homepage_continuous_scroll_scaffold_plan.md`.

Required plan contents:
1. Proposed section map in order (e.g. Hero, Value Pillars, Feature Strips, Ecosystem/Proof, CTA Footer).
2. Interaction scaffold (scroll progression, sticky section nav/"On this page", active section state, smooth anchor jumps).
3. Responsive behavior (desktop section rail vs mobile condensed nav).
4. Performance/accessibility constraints (semantic sections, reduced-motion support, image loading strategy, keyboard/anchor navigation).
5. File/module scaffolding aligned to current feature-based structure (front-end/src/features/home/* + shared primitives).
6. Test strategy for scaffold behavior without final content (render tests, nav/anchor behavior checks, basic accessibility assertions).

Acceptance criteria:
- Written plan committed in-repo as `homepage_continuous_scroll_scaffold_plan.md`.
- Plan references observed patterns from the two GitHub repositories above and best-practice navigation guidance.
- Plan is implementation-ready for a follow-up task.
